title: Canonical derived section comparisons commute with weakly etale localization.
statement: For a commutative condensed ring Λ, quotient closed immersion s, cartesian closed-fibre square (f,h,fZ,s), and an affine closed-site test V, the canonical derived section maps of [def-sfb-closed-test-localized-model-data] satisfy the three localization computation and section-diagram clauses needed for GeometricCoherence. Explicitly: weakly etale base change of each of f,h,fZ,s preserves K-injectives under source restriction and the exchange is invertible; its representative formula is the ordinary unit-normalized mate. Localized restriction along closedFibreMap commutes with a cartesian weakly etale localization square. The canonical sectionComparison also commutes with every compatible cartesian localization cube for f and fZ, including all pullback composition constraints. This assertion concerns canonical derived section maps, independently of any representative I,J or modelArrow. The canonical mate unit and counit equations of LocalizationAdjunction are part of this statement; they follow from the defining adjunct formula and triangle identities.

proof.text:
Weakly etale localization identifies the pro-etale sites with slices. Transport
internal modules to section-ring modules using the exact section-preserving equivalence.
Apply the ringed-sheaf-slice derived comparison to each cartesian square. Restriction
has an exact left adjoint and therefore preserves K-injectives; its comparison with
derived direct image is invertible and has the stated representative formula. The mate
counit equation is supplied by that comparison. Transpose it using the triangle
identities to get the displayed unit equation. This proves LocalizationAdjunction.
For the restriction square, compose the ordinary units for the two successive inverse
images and use pullback composition to identify the equal composite scheme maps.
For the localization cube, evaluate both composites on a K-injective representative.
Each is the same fibre-product section map, and the normalized derived direct-image
composition carries that equality to the asserted cube. Exact pullback composition
retains every coefficient constraint. The argument works for arbitrary squares,
so the four specified global arrows and isomorphisms of squares are included.
 The input declarations are [lem-sbc-ringed-topos-sheaf-slice-derived-comparison], [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction].
